text: FACT crashes resulting from improper passing [?often] result in head-on crashes AND can be deadly

flags.note: Hedged generalisation.

text: DEFINE overtaking IS passing THAT goes past the vehicle ahead

sources.quote: overtake – to pass the vehicle ahead
sources.where: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › O · ¶4 (PDF p. 80)

flags.note: The handbook uses "pass", "overtake" and "overtaking and passing" for the same manoeuvre; the statements write "pass".
flags.zh: 手冊對同一個動作混用 "pass"、"overtake" 和 "overtaking and passing"；規則一律寫 "pass"。

note: The glossary entry is the handbook's only definition of passing; chapter 6 (Passing) has none. Elsewhere "pass" also means going by (a school bus on a different road, 3.4.12c), and the glossary limits overtaking to the vehicle ahead.
note_zh: 詞彙表這一條是手冊對超車唯一的定義；第 6 章（Passing）沒有定義。手冊別處的 "pass" 也指從旁經過（例如經過另一條道路上的校車，3.4.12c），而詞彙表把 overtaking 限定為超越前方車輛。

text: a driver SHOULD keep to the right side of the road UNLESS the driver is passing another vehicle on a two- or three-lane street OR the driver is on a one-way street OR the right side of the road is blocked

sources.where: Chapter 6: Signaling, Passing, and Turning › Passing › Keep to the Right · item 6 (PDF p. 44)

flags.span: Keep to the right of the yellow center line
flags.note: The pavement-marking page restates it for two-lane roads as keeping right of the yellow centre line, and lets a driver cross a broken line to pass (3.1.6a).
flags.zh: 標線頁針對雙車道道路重述為「靠黃色中線右側行駛」，並允許超車時跨越虛線（3.1.6a）。

note: The list lead "except when:" introduces alternative exceptions, so the three items are one UNLESS clause joined by OR.
note_zh: 清單引言 "except when:" 帶出的是擇一的例外，所以這三項合成一個 UNLESS 子句，用 OR 連接。

text: a driver SHOULD be patient AND wait WHEN the driver is about to pass UNTIL the time is [?right] BECAUSE it is not always [?safe] to pass

sources.quote: It is not always safe to pass. Be patient and wait until the time is right.
sources.where: Chapter 6: Signaling, Passing, and Turning › Passing › Basic Safety Rules When You Are Passing · ¶1 (PDF p. 44)

flags.note: No test for when the time is right.
flags.zh: 沒有說怎樣算時機「對」。

flags.note: Judgment term.
flags.zh: 判斷詞，沒有可觀察的標準。

note: The condition comes from the heading "Basic Safety Rules When You Are Passing"; "It is not always safe to pass" is written as the reason.
note_zh: 條件來自標題 "Basic Safety Rules When You Are Passing"；"It is not always safe to pass" 寫成理由。

text: a driver SHOULD pass ONLY IF the way is [?clear]

sources.quote: Make certain the way is clear.
sources.where: Chapter 6: Signaling, Passing, and Turning › Passing › Basic Safety Rules When You Are Passing · item 1 (PDF p. 44)

flags.note: No test for how clear the way must be.
flags.zh: 沒有說道路要淨空到什麼程度。

note: Under the heading "Basic Safety Rules When You Are Passing". "Make certain" is the imperative itself and, like "be sure" elsewhere, is not flagged separately.
note_zh: 位在標題 "Basic Safety Rules When You Are Passing" 底下。"Make certain" 本身就是祈使語，和別處的 "be sure" 一樣，不另外標記。

text: a driver SHOULD give the [?proper] signal WHEN about to change lanes to pass

sources.quote: Give the proper signal before changing lanes.
sources.where: Chapter 6: Signaling, Passing, and Turning › Passing › Basic Safety Rules When You Are Passing · item 2 (PDF p. 44)

flags.note: The handbook does not say which signal is proper here; the two-lane procedure (2.2a) says the left turn signal.
flags.zh: 這裡沒說哪種信號才算「適當」；雙車道超車程序（2.2a）說的是左轉方向燈。

note: Restates step 1 of 2.2a as a rule that holds on its own.
note_zh: 把 2.2a 的第 1 步重述成可以單獨成立的規則。

text: a driver SHOULD tap the horn WHEN passing AND this is [?necessary] to avoid surprising the driver ahead

sources.quote: Tap your horn when necessary to avoid surprising the driver ahead.
sources.where: Chapter 6: Signaling, Passing, and Turning › Passing › Basic Safety Rules When You Are Passing · item 3 (PDF p. 44)

sources.quote: Tap your horn when necessary to alert the driver ahead.
sources.where: Chapter 6: Signaling, Passing, and Turning › Passing › How to Pass on a Two-Lane Road · item 3 (PDF p. 45)

flags.note: Who judges necessity, and how, is not stated.
flags.zh: 沒說由誰、依什麼判斷是否「必要」。

flags.note: The two-lane procedure (2.2a step 3) gives the purpose as alerting the driver ahead.
flags.zh: 雙車道超車程序（2.2a 第 3 步）把目的寫成「提醒前車駕駛」。

note: Stated in the basic safety rules and again as step 3 of 2.2a; the two passages are joined.
note_zh: 基本安全規則裡寫過一次，2.2a 第 3 步又寫一次；兩段合併成一條。

text: a driver SHOULD NOT cut in [?too quickly] WHEN returning to the original lane after passing

sources.quote: Avoid cutting in too quickly if you must return to your original lane.
sources.where: Chapter 6: Signaling, Passing, and Turning › Passing › Basic Safety Rules When You Are Passing · item 4 (PDF p. 44)

flags.note: No gap or time given.
flags.zh: 沒有給間距或時間。

text: TO pass a vehicle WHEN on a two-lane road

sources.quote: Diagram: a car passes another car on a two-lane road, moving into the left lane and back to the right lane
sources.where: Chapter 6: Signaling, Passing, and Turning › Passing › How to Pass on a Two-Lane Road · image (PDF p. 45)

flags.note: No distance, time or space given.
flags.zh: 沒有給距離、時間或空間。

flags.note: Subjective certainty; no observable test.
flags.zh: 主觀的確定感，沒有可觀察的檢驗方式。

flags.note: No test for when the road is clear.
flags.zh: 沒有說怎樣算道路淨空。

flags.note: No distance given.
flags.zh: 沒有給距離。

flags.note: Who judges necessity is not stated.
flags.zh: 沒說由誰判斷是否必要。

flags.note: Judgment term.
flags.zh: 判斷詞，沒有可觀察的標準。

note: The condition comes from the heading "How to Pass on a Two-Lane Road"; on a two-lane road the handbook's "right lane" is the original lane. Texas numbers every list, but this one is a real sequence ("How to Pass"), so it is one PROCEDURE. The diagram shows a car moving into the left lane, past another car and back.
note_zh: 條件來自標題 "How to Pass on a Two-Lane Road"；在雙車道道路上，手冊說的 "right lane" 就是原車道。德州手冊每個清單都有編號，但這一份確實是依序的步驟（"How to Pass"），所以寫成一個 PROCEDURE。示意圖畫的是一輛車駛入左側車道，超越另一輛車後再回到原車道。

steps.text: keep [?enough] distance behind the vehicle ahead to see ahead clearly AND check the inside mirror, the side mirrors and the blind spot over the shoulder to make [?sure] the road is [?clear] and no other vehicle is passing the driver AND turn on the left turn signal to alert drivers behind

check [?well ahead] for signs and pavement markings for no-passing zones AND check for oncoming traffic in the left lane AND be [?sure] there is [?enough] time and space to pass the vehicle ahead and return to the original lane before an approaching vehicle comes within 200 ft
tap the horn WHEN [?necessary] to alert the driver ahead
pass on the left AND do not return to the original lane UNTIL the driver has [?safely] cleared the vehicle being passed AND the vehicle being passed is visible in the inside mirror
turn on the right turn signal AND return to the original lane AND turn off the signal once the lane change is complete

text: a driver SHOULD pass WHEN on a two-lane road ONLY IF the driver has [?enough] time and space to pass the vehicle ahead and return to the original lane before an approaching vehicle comes within 200 ft

sources.quote: Be sure you have enough time and space to overtake the car ahead and return to the right lane before an approaching car comes within 200 feet of you.
sources.where: Chapter 6: Signaling, Passing, and Turning › Passing › How to Pass on a Two-Lane Road · item 2 (PDF p. 45)

flags.note: No time or space given apart from the 200 ft margin.
flags.zh: 除了 200 英尺的餘裕外，沒有給時間或空間。

flags.note: A fixed distance in a bare imperative reads like a legal limit, but the sentence has no legal wording.
flags.zh: 祈使句中出現固定距離，讀來像法定限制，但句子沒有法律用語。

note: Also step 2 of 2.2a; written as its own rule because the 200 ft margin holds whatever the step order.
note_zh: 也是 2.2a 的第 2 步；另寫成獨立規則，是因為 200 ft 的餘裕不論步驟順序都成立。

force_from: imperative ("do not drive or linger", "Either pass … or slow down")
text: a driver SHOULD NOT drive or linger in the other driver's blind spot AND SHOULD pass the other driver or slow down WHILE passing BECAUSE the other driver [?likely] cannot see the vehicle in or near the blind spot

sources.quote: When you are passing, do not drive or linger in the other driver’s blind spot. Either pass the other driver or slow down so you are not in another driver’s blind spot. It is likely the other driver cannot see you if you are in or near their blind spot.
sources.where: Chapter 6: Signaling, Passing, and Turning › Passing › Blind Spot Driving · ¶1 (PDF p. 45)

sources.quote: Blind Spot
sources.where: Chapter 6: Signaling, Passing, and Turning › Passing › Blind Spot Driving · image (PDF p. 45)

sources.quote: Stay out of another driver’s blind spot. Traveling where the driver ahead of you cannot see your vehicle can be dangerous. Stay behind or go around the other vehicle. Do not follow to the side.
sources.where: Chapter 9: Some Special Driving Situations › Highway Driving › Highway Safety Tips · item 3 (PDF p. 54)

flags.note: Hedged: "It is likely" the other driver cannot see.
flags.zh: 保留語氣：原文說「很可能」看不到。

flags.span: Stay behind or go around the other vehicle. Do not follow to the side.
flags.note: Highway Safety Tips (ch. 9) give the rule for all driving, not only while passing, and word it as staying behind or going around.
flags.zh: 第 9 章公路安全提示把這條寫成所有駕駛情況都適用（不只超車時），用語是「留在後方或繞過去」。

note: Two passages state the rule and are joined; WHILE passing comes from the chapter 6 sentence. The diagram shows a car with shaded blind-spot areas behind it on both sides.
note_zh: 兩段原文都講這條規則，合併成一條；WHILE passing 來自第 6 章的那一句。示意圖畫的是一輛車，車後兩側有塗上陰影的盲點區域。

text: DEFINE a blind spot IS an area THAT the mirrors cannot show

sources.quote: blind spot – an area rearview mirrors cannot show
sources.where: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › B · ¶4 (PDF p. 77)

flags.note: The glossary says "rearview mirrors" for all the mirrors; chapter 6 uses "rearview mirror" for the inside mirror and "side mirrors" for the others.
flags.zh: 詞彙表用 "rearview mirrors" 泛指所有後照鏡；第 6 章則用 "rearview mirror" 指車內後視鏡，另以 "side mirrors" 指側鏡。

note: Needed to read 2.3a and the blind-spot checks in 2.2a and 3.4.6a.
note_zh: 要讀懂 2.3a，以及 2.2a 和 3.4.6a 裡的盲點檢查，需要這條定義。

sources.where: Appendix C › Study and Review Questions for Class C Operators · item 63 (PDF p. 85)

flags.span: on the left side of the road
flags.note: Bans the means (driving left of centre), not passing as such; the heading Passing › Keep to the Right and study question 63 tie it to passing.
flags.zh: 禁止的是手段（開到道路左側），不是超車本身；標題「Passing › Keep to the Right」和第 63 題把它跟超車連在一起。

flags.note: No measure of how limited vision must be.
flags.zh: 沒有說視線受限到什麼程度才算。

flags.note: Fixed distances under a bare "Never" read like a legal limit, and item 1 speaks of markings and signs that prohibit; the sentence itself has no legal wording.
flags.zh: 單純的 "Never" 句中出現固定距離，讀來像法定限制，第 1 項也說標線或標誌「禁止」；但句子本身沒有法律用語。

flags.note: Study question 24 asks the same distance for "the left half of the roadway" near an intersection, bridge or railroad crossing.
flags.zh: 第 24 題用 "the left half of the roadway"（道路左半邊）問同一個距離，地點是路口、橋梁或鐵路平交道。

note: The list lead "Never drive on the left side of the road when:" introduces alternative conditions, so the five items make one statement joined by OR. It is filed under 3.1 because the items span bridges (3.1.2), hills and curves (3.1.3), markings (3.1.5), signs (3.1.7) and intersections and railroad crossings (3.1.8). Sources p142 and p143 are study questions; keep it out of the rule set if that page is used for evaluation.
note_zh: 清單引言 "Never drive on the left side of the road when:" 帶出的是擇一的條件，所以這五項合成一條敘述，用 OR 連接。歸在 3.1 之下，是因為這些項目橫跨橋梁（3.1.2）、坡道與彎道（3.1.3）、標線（3.1.5）、標誌（3.1.7）以及交叉路口與鐵路平交道（3.1.8）。來源 p142 和 p143 是練習題；若評估時會用到那一頁，就不要把這條納入規則集。

flags.note: Highway Driving (ch. 9) words it as using the right lane at the minimum posted speed or below the normal flow of traffic.
flags.zh: 第 9 章公路駕駛把它寫成：以最低速限或低於一般車流的速度行駛時使用右側車道。

note: Two passages give the same advice and are joined. The legal form, where the sign is posted, is 3.6.1a.
note_zh: 兩段原文給出相同的建議，合併成一條。設有標誌時的法規版本是 3.6.1a。

text: a driver being passed SHOULD NOT increase speed WHILE another vehicle is passing

sources.quote: Do not increase your speed.
sources.where: Chapter 6: Signaling, Passing, and Turning › Passing › When Another Vehicle is Passing · item 1 (PDF p. 45)

sources.quote: Don’t speed up while the truck is passing.
sources.where: Chapter 9: Some Special Driving Situations › Share the Road with Trucks (Large trucks and truck-tractor combinations) › Passing · item 4 (PDF p. 57)

flags.span: Don’t speed up while the truck is passing.
flags.note: Repeated in the truck section for a truck that is passing.
flags.zh: 卡車一節針對卡車超車時重複了這一條。

note: The condition comes from the heading "When Another Vehicle is Passing".
note_zh: 條件來自標題 "When Another Vehicle is Passing"。

text: a driver being passed SHOULD stay in the driver's lane WHILE another vehicle is passing

sources.quote: Stay in your lane.
sources.where: Chapter 6: Signaling, Passing, and Turning › Passing › When Another Vehicle is Passing · item 2 (PDF p. 45)

note: The condition comes from the heading "When Another Vehicle is Passing".
note_zh: 條件來自標題 "When Another Vehicle is Passing"。

text: a driver being passed SHOULD make it as [?safe and easy as possible] for the other driver to pass WHILE another vehicle is passing

sources.quote: Make it as safe and easy as possible for the other driver to pass you.
sources.where: Chapter 6: Signaling, Passing, and Turning › Passing › When Another Vehicle is Passing · item 4 (PDF p. 45)

flags.note: No observable test.
flags.zh: 沒有可觀察的標準。

text: a driver MUST NOT use the vehicle in an attempt to prevent another vehicle from passing IF VIOLATED a criminal penalty ranging from a Class B misdemeanor to a second-degree felony AND automatic suspension of the driver license

sources.quote: A person may not participate in:
sources.where: Chapter 8: Speed and Speed Limits › Street Racing · ¶4 (PDF p. 52)

sources.quote: A race;
sources.where: Chapter 8: Speed and Speed Limits › Street Racing · item 1 (PDF p. 52)

sources.quote: race – the use of one or more vehicles in an attempt to:
sources.where: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › R · ¶1 (PDF p. 80)

sources.quote: Out gain or outdistance another vehicle or prevent another vehicle from passing;
sources.where: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › R · item 1 (PDF p. 80)

sources.quote: The criminal penalty for a conviction of Speed Racing ranges from a Class B misdemeanor to a second-degree felony.
sources.where: Chapter 8: Speed and Speed Limits › Street Racing · ¶5 (PDF p. 52)

sources.quote: Convictions for the following offenses will result in the automatic suspension of your license and driving privilege.
sources.where: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Suspensions and Revocations › Mandatory Suspension · ¶1 (PDF p. 16)

sources.quote: Racing a motor vehicle on a public highway or street
sources.where: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Suspensions and Revocations › Mandatory Suspension · item 20 (PDF p. 17)

flags.span: speed up to keep someone from passing
flags.note: The road-rage tips (3.6.1h) advise against the same act without legal force.
flags.zh: 防止路怒的提示（3.6.1h）也勸人別這樣做，但沒有法律效力。

note: The street-racing law forbids taking part in a race, and the glossary defines a race to include using a vehicle to prevent another vehicle from passing (3.6.1i); the passages are joined. The penalty sentence calls the offense "Speed Racing"; the mandatory-suspension list says "Racing a motor vehicle on a public highway or street".
note_zh: 街頭競速法禁止參與競速，而詞彙表對競速的定義包括用車輛阻止其他車輛超車（3.6.1i）；這幾段合併成一條。罰則那一句把這項違規叫作 "Speed Racing"；強制吊扣清單則寫 "Racing a motor vehicle on a public highway or street"。

text: a driver in any lane other than the right-hand lane SHOULD be prepared to move to another lane to allow faster traffic to pass WHEN driving on a highway

sources.quote: Vehicles in any lane, except the right lane used for slower traffic, should be prepared to move to another lane to allow faster traffic to pass.
sources.where: Chapter 9: Some Special Driving Situations › Highway Driving › Driving on the Highway › Once You are in the Proper Lane · item 6 (PDF p. 54)

note: The handbook says "vehicles in any lane, except the right lane used for slower traffic"; the role is their drivers. The condition comes from the heading Highway Driving.
note_zh: 手冊寫的是 "vehicles in any lane, except the right lane used for slower traffic"；規則的對象是這些車輛的駕駛人。條件來自標題 Highway Driving。

text: a driver SHOULD NOT intentionally slow down, slam on the brakes or speed up to keep another driver from passing or entering the driver's lane

sources.quote: Do not intentionally slow down, slam on your brakes, or speed up to keep someone from passing or entering your lane of travel.
sources.where: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Road Rage › Tips to Avoid Road Rage · item 5 (PDF p. 72)

flags.note: The glossary's definition of a race covers the same act, which the street-racing law forbids (3.6.1f).
flags.zh: 詞彙表對「競速」的定義涵蓋同一行為，而街頭競速法禁止此行為（3.6.1f）。

note: Listed as a road-rage tip; "entering your lane of travel" is not about passing but is part of the same sentence.
note_zh: 列為防止路怒的提示之一；"entering your lane of travel" 與超車無關，但屬於同一句。

text: DEFINE a race IS the use of one or more vehicles THAT includes an attempt to out gain or outdistance another vehicle or to prevent another vehicle from passing

sources.quote: race – the use of one or more vehicles in an attempt to:
sources.where: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › R · ¶1 (PDF p. 80)

sources.quote: Out gain or outdistance another vehicle or prevent another vehicle from passing;
sources.where: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › R · item 1 (PDF p. 80)

note: Only the first item of the glossary's list is selected; the other two (arriving ahead of another vehicle, testing endurance) are not about passing.
note_zh: 只取詞彙表清單的第一項；另外兩項（比其他車輛先抵達、測試耐力）與超車無關。

text: a driver being passed SHOULD move [?as far to the right as the driver can] [?safely] WHEN being passed on the left AND the lanes are not marked

sources.quote: Safely move as far to the right as you can when being passed on the left and the lanes are not marked.
sources.where: Chapter 6: Signaling, Passing, and Turning › Passing › When Another Vehicle is Passing · item 3 (PDF p. 45)

flags.span: as far to the right as the driver can
flags.note: No distance given; the handbook says "as far to the right as you can".
flags.zh: 沒有給距離；原文是 "as far to the right as you can"。

flags.note: Judgment term.
flags.zh: 判斷詞，沒有可觀察的標準。

note: Filed under 3.6.2 (being passed on an undivided road): the Texas condition is unmarked lanes.
note_zh: 歸在 3.6.2（在無分隔道路上被超車）之下：德州的條件是車道沒有標線。
